definitions.explanation: An activity or entertainment that takes one's mind off worries or boredom. Implies a pleasant, refreshing change of pace rather than deep engagement.

examples.japanese: {気散|きさん}じに{散歩|さんぽ}に{出|で}かけた。
examples.english: I went for a walk as a diversion.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}の{合間|あいま}に{気散|きさん}じに{本|ほん}を{読|よ}んでいる。
examples.english: I read books as a diversion between work tasks.

examples.japanese: {看病|かんびょう}{疲|つか}れの{母|はは}に、{少|すこ}しでも{気散|きさん}じになればと{映画|えいが}のチケットを{贈|おく}った。
examples.english: I gave movie tickets to my mother, who was exhausted from nursing care, hoping it would be a nice distraction.

notes:
Composed of {気|き} (spirit/mood) + {散|さん} (scatter) + じ (a classical suffix). Literally "scattering one's spirit," meaning to relieve mental tension through a pleasant activity. Has an old-fashioned, slightly literary flavor.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {気散|きさん}じに: as a diversion; for amusement
- {気散|きさん}じになる: to serve as a distraction
- {気散|きさん}じにする: to do something for diversion

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {気分転換|きぶんてんかん}: change of pace; mood refresh — the modern, everyday equivalent
- {暇潰|ひまつぶ}し: killing time — more casual, implies boredom rather than stress relief
- {娯楽|ごらく}: entertainment; recreation — broader term for leisure activities in general
